title: Television: James Paul McCartney | 1973
content:
Filming for the television special James Paul McCartney continued on 25 March 1973 at Elstree Studios.

This day’s filming was for sequences in which Wings mimed to audio of ‘My Love’ and ‘Live And Let Die’ that had been recorded at Elstree earlier in the month.

The staging of ‘Live And Let Die’ was the more elaborate of the two. During the song’s ending, the camera cut to a figure in the studio rafters who pressed down on a dynamite detonator. Paul McCartney’s piano – a prop partly made of balsa wood – exploded.

They told us, ‘When we get to the end of the song, there’s going to be a blast – the piano is going to break apart in the middle and fall in on itself, so be aware of it. But I don’t think they told the violin section, which was behind the piano. These are all old guys, with toupees, holding their Stradivariuses. Well, the blast was bigger than they expected. The piano broke in half, and it was like a ball of flames, and pieces of wood went up and over these violin players’ heads. I’m surprised somebody didn’t have a heart attack. It was such a blast that Henry was standing next to Paul, and it swept him off his feet. I was hiding behind the cymbals, trying not to get hurt.
Denny Seiwell, 6 June 2016
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 1: 1969-73
